Pursuant to Table 3.02.05-1, Footnote #3, Notwithstanding Section 1.02.E.2, a site plan or site plan amendment application for minor changes to an approved site plan for a data center use may be permitted without a SPEX approval. EPLAN-2026-0053, Brambleton Tech Park Site Plan Amendment was accepted for review on June 16, 2026, and is a site plan amendment for the proposed revisions discussed in your May 1, 2026, request letter. As depicted in EPLAN-2026-0053 and detailed in your request letter, the proposed site design changes consist of addition of switchgear equipment; installation of a retaining wall along the western property frontage; minor adjustments to the parking configuration adjacent to the two southern buildings; and changes to the cooling tanks at the end of the building, resulting in minor modifications to the associated drive aisle configuration and on-site circulation. Your letter indicates these changes are necessary to facilitate a functional and constructable site layout based on final engineering and vehicular circulation. 

Section 10.11.01.H.2. allows the Zoning Administrator to permit minor changes to an approved SPEX when such are reasonably necessary to address issues related to topography, drainage, underground utilities, structural safety, final engineering, vehicular circulation, or requirements of government agencies. Based on the site revisions described in your May 1, 2026, request letter and as depicted on EPLAN-2026-0053, staff find the site design changes are related to minor changes reasonably necessary to address issues related to final engineering and vehicular circulation. Therefore, the requested minor changes to STMP-2022-0018 are consistent with the provisions of Section 10.11.01.H.2. and are hereby granted as depicted in the exhibit provided with the May 1, 2026, request letter and in EPLAN-2026-0053.

As is detailed in Footnote #3 to Table 3.02.05-1 of the Zoning Ordinance, a site plan amendment application for minor changes to an approved site plan for a data center use (such approved site plan being EPLAN-2023-0087 in this case) is permitted without processing a Special Exception application, so long as the proposed changes are in conformance with Section 10.11.01.H of the Zoning Ordinance. 

More specifically, Section 10.11.01.H.2. of the Zoning Ordinance states, the Zoning Administrator may permit minor changes to an approved Special Exception when such are reasonably necessary to address issues related to topography, drainage, underground utilities, structural safety, final engineering, vehicular circulation, or requirements of government agencies. As confirmed by County Staff, under this scenario, EPLAN-2023-0087 (the Approved Site Plan) operates as the approved Special Exception for purposes of Section 10. As detailed within the plans submitted as part of EPLAN-2025-0149, the amendment proposes to slightly adjust the location of several improvements on the Property from what was originally shown on the Approved Site Plan, including the drive aisle and the building footprint. These changes are necessary following a final engineering analysis, which determined that the retaining wall shown on the Approved Site Plan is not constructible in its initially proposed location. As a result of moving the retaining wall, the originally contemplated location of the nearby drive aisle also requires a minor relocation. Zoning Determination requesting confirmation that (i) data centers are permitted in the GI district pursuant to Section 3.02.05 of the 2023 Zoning Ordinance; (ii) ZMAP-1986-0019, specifically Proffer #1, does not prohibit the development of data centers on the Property; and (iii) no legislative approvals are necessary in order to develop the Property with data center uses in accordance with the GI zoning district under the 2023 Zoning Ordinance.

2/24/2025
By way of background, the Subject Property is currently zoned GI (General Industry),
administered under the Loudoun County Zoning Ordinance (Zoning Ordinance), adopted December 13, 2023. The Subject Property is within the Airport Impact Overlay District (AIOD) located between the ldn 60-65 aircraft noise contours, subject to Section 5.02 of the Zoning Ordinance. Additionally, the Subject Property is within the Route 28 Tax District. 
The Subject Property is subject to the Proffer Statement and Concept Development Plan (CDP) associated with Zoning Map Amendment (ZMAP)-1986-0019, Evans-Cockerille, approved on September 21, 1987. Further a Site Plan (STPL)-1998-0093, was approved on February 10, 1999, for a Storage Facility with accessory Office use.

(i) Data Centers are permitted in the GI zoning district pursuant to Section 3.02.05 of the 2023 Zoning Ordinance.
Pursuant to Chapter 3, Section 3.02, Table 3.02.05-01 of the Zoning Ordinance, data center is a permitted use in the GI zoning district, subject to the Use-Specific Standards of Chapter 4, Section 4.06.02. 
(ii) ZMAP-1986-0019, specifically Proffer #1, does not prohibit the development of data center uses on the property.
Proffer # I.1., approved with ZMAP-1986-0019 states, in part, the applicant will develop the property in accord with the regulations of the PD-GI district, except that commercial office uses will be limited to flex/industrial offices and will conform to the following criteria. Proffer # I. 1., restricts primary office uses, certain types of office use (corporate headquarters (not associated with permitted uses), law offices, architectural offices, insurance offices, medical offices and health maintenance organizations) and some additional uses (dry cleaning plant, commercial repair garage, frozen food locker, radio & television broadcasting, relay station) otherwise permitted in the GI zoning district. 
However, Proffer # I.1, does not prohibit data center use. A data center use is categorized as an industrial/production use in the Zoning Ordinance. 
Pursuant to Chapter 12, Definitions, Data Center is defined as:
An establishment engaging in the storage, management, processing, and/or 
transmission of digital data, and housing computer and/or network equipment, 
systems, servers, appliances and other associated components related to digital data operations.
(iii) no legislative approvals are necessary in order to develop the property with data center uses in accordance with the GI zoning district under the 2023 Loudoun County Zoning Ordinance.
Pursuant to Chapter 3, Section 3.02, Table 3.02.05-01 of the Zoning Ordinance data center is a permitted use in the GI zoning district, subject to the Use-Specific Standards of Section 4.06.02. Further, as discussed above, Proffer I.1. does not specify the prohibition of data center uses. Therefore, at the time of this letter, no legislative approvals are necessary to develop data center uses on the Subject Property. However, please be advised that Loudoun County is currently considering a Zoning Ordinance Amendment (ZOAM-2024-0001) to amend the Zoning Ordinance to require a special exception for data center uses in the GI, IP (Industrial Park) and MR-HI (Mineral Resource-Heavy Industry) zoning districts. Be advised that action on this item will affect the permissibility of data center uses on the Subject Property. 
Please note data center use is permitted in the GI zoning district subject to the Use Specific Standards of Chapter 4, Section 4.06.02 attached herein (Attachment 1). The applicant must demonstrate conformance to the standards of Section 4.06.02 at the Site Plan approval. You can also access Chapter 4 of the Zoning Ordinance here: Loudoun County, VA Zoning Ordinance. At a minimum, in order to establish the data center use on the Subject Property, a site plan pursuant to Section 10.06 and a zoning permit pursuant to Section 10.04 are required. Please contact the Department of Building and Development at 703-777-0220 (Option # 1) for additional information.

Section 10.11.01.H. of the Zoning Ordinance allows for minor changes after approval
of a SPEX. Such minor changes are permitted when they are reasonably necessary 
to address issues related to topography, drainage, underground utilities, structural 
safety, final engineering, vehicular circulation, or requirements of government 
agencies. These changes may include the addition of accessory structures that are 
clearly subordinate to the approved SPEX use; the realignment of principal buildings
and parking areas within an approved building envelope; or minor additions to principal buildings and corresponding additions to parking areas, provided the 
cumulative total of all building additions neither exceed 5% of the existing gross floor 
area; nor exceed maximum permitted floor area ratio for the zoning district. Also, 
the Zoning Ordinance defines an Accessory Structure as a building or structure 
subordinate and incidental to, and located on the same lot with, a principal building, 
the use of which is customarily found in association with and is clearly incidental to 
that of the main building or to the use of the land, and is not attached by any part of 
a common wall or roof to the principal building.

The construction of an additional data center building within the existing data center 
development does not meet these criteria. The proposed data center building cannot
be considered an addition to an existing building given that it is a separate detached 
structure. It also cannot be considered an accessory structure as it is not subordinate, but rather an expansion, to the data center use on the property.

By way of background, the above referenced property (the Property) is split zoned 
Industrial Park (IP) and General Industry (GI) under the Loudoun County Zoning 
Ordinance. The IP portion of the Property is developed with existing data center use. 
The GI portion of the Property (Project Aspen Site) is the location of the Project 
Aspen data center that is subject to EPLAN-2024-0139 and this determination 
request. The Project Aspen Site is subject to Zoning Map Amendment (ZMAP)-2019-
0003 and Special Exception (SPEX)-2019-0003, Luck/Hayden/Loudoun Water 
Property approved February 18, 2020. EPLAN-2023-0128, Project Aspen, was 
approved November 15, 2024, for a single data center on the Project Aspen Site. 
EPLAN-2024-0139, Project Aspen, proposes a revision to approved EPLAN-2023-0128 to adjust the mechanical yard on the east side of the proposed Project Aspen data center building per new specifications provided by the Owner.

Staff notes EPLAN-2023-0128 was processed, reviewed, and approved under the land 
use and development regulations prescribed in the Revised 1993 Zoning Ordinance
pursuant to the Resolution of the Board of Supervisors of Loudoun County Virginia, 
Adopting Grandfathering Rules for ZOAM-2020-0001, Zoning Ordinance Rewrite 
(Grandfathering Resolution), adopted on December 13, 2023. EPLAN-2024-0138 is 
being processed and reviewed under the land use and development regulations 
prescribed in the Zoning Ordinance since EPLAN-2024-0138 was submitted after 
December 13, 2023 and is subject to the data center use specific standards in Zoning 
Ordinance Section 4.06.02. 

Table 4.06.02-2.b.1.d. of the Zoning Ordinance states the following:
No Screening Requirements Adjacent to Industrially Zoned Property.
As determined by the Zoning Administrator, Data Center Mechanical 
Equipment located in a manner found to have no adverse impact on adjacent 
properties zoned IP, GI, or MR-HI is not required to be screened pursuant to 
Section 4.06.02-2.b.1, except that Data Center Mechanical Equipment must 
be screened from any existing or planned public road.
Per the Countys geographic information system, WebLOGIS, the adjacent parcel 
information is as follows:
North: PIN: 152-25-4491, zoned MR-HI under the Zoning Ordinance. 
East: PIN: 152-26-8334, zoned GI under the Zoning Ordinance. 
South: PIN: 153-35-5865, zoned MR-HI under the Zoning Ordinance. 
West: PIN: 193-18-6982, zoned IP under the Zoning Ordinance. 
The adjacent parcel to the north, PIN: 152-25-4491, is currently vacant. The Project 
Aspen Site contains required buffer yard plantings as well as proffered reforestation 
area #1 along the northern property line. As such, Zoning Administration staff finds 
the mechanical equipment yard is located in a manner found to have no adverse 
impact on the adjacent parcel to the north zoned MR-HI.
The adjacent parcel to the east, PIN: 152-26-8334, is currently vacant. The Project 
Aspen Site contains a proffered Tree Conservation Area along the entirety of the 
eastern property line adjacent to PIN: 152-26-8334. As such, Zoning Administration 
staff finds the mechanical yard is located in a manner found to have no adverse 
impact on the adjacent parcel to the east zoned GI.
The adjacent parcel to the south, PIN: 153-35-5865, is currently improved with an 
existing Water Treatment Plant. Staff notes when EPLAN-2023-0128 was approved, 
a buffer yard was not required between the proposed Project Aspen data center 
(Group 10 buffer use group) and the existing Water Treatment Plant (Group 10 buffer 
use group). However, EPLAN-2023-0128 proposed to retain existing vegetation as 
Tree Conservation Area (Tree Conservation Area 3) along the southern property line 
adjacent to PIN: 153-35-5865. EPLAN-2024-0138 continues to depict Tree 
Conservation Area 3 along the southern property line adjacent to PIN: 153-35-5865. 
As such, Zoning Administration staff finds the mechanical yard is located in a manner 
found to have no adverse impact on the adjacent parcel to the south zoned MR-HI.
In regard to the visual impact on the Dulles Greenway, the southern property line of 
the Project Aspen Site adjacent to the Dulles Greenway contains a proffered Tree 
Conservation Area as depicted on Sheet 3A-C-9700 of EPLAN-2024-0139 and in lineof-sight elevation 03. Additionally, the Project Aspen Site contains proffered 
reforestation area #2 north of said proffered Tree Conservation Area. The Project 
Aspen data center building will also provide screening of the mechanical yard from 
the Dulles Greenway. As such, Zoning Administration staff finds the mechanical yard 
is sufficiently screened from the Dulles Greenway. 
The adjacent parcel to the west, PIN: 193-18-6982, has approved land development 
applications for data center development. Further, the existing data center use 
located on the IP portion of the Property is located between the Project Aspen Site 
and PIN: 193-18-6982. The Project Aspen mechanical yard is located behind the 
Project Aspen data center building to the east. As such, Zoning Administration staff 
finds the mechanical yard is located in a manner found to have no adverse impact on 
the adjacent property to the west zoned IP.
